# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller: achievement manifest entry + Steamworks API name

## Problem Statement

The new **Serial Seller** challenge (`ch-serial-seller`) must map to a persistent Steam achievement like the existing 12 challenges. The challenge-side mapping is added in the parent item (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J); this item covers the cross-repo pieces required before the parent can be reviewed.

## Users

- **Producers**: Need the Steam achievement registered on the Steamworks partner backend.
- **Developers**: Need the manifest entry to exist before the drift guard test will pass.
- **Players**: Need the Serial Seller achievement to appear in-game alongside the existing 12 achievements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains a `serial-seller` entry with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false`.
2. The Steamworks partner backend declares the matching `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` achievement API name.
3. The `core` submodule pointer in the main-street repo is bumped to the commit containing the manifest change.
4. The manifest drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) passes with the parent's mapping in place.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The manifest lives in the `core` git submodule (a separate repository: `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`), requiring two repo operations.
- The `steamApiName` values must match exactly what is configured on the Steamworks partner backend, or Steam will silently drop the unlock.
- The achievement must not be hidden (`hidden: false`), consistent with the existing 12 challenges.
- The Steamworks backend configuration is a producer/external action that must be completed independently of code changes.

## Existing State

- 12 existing achievements in `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`, all with the pattern `TCE_MAIN_STREET_<UPPER_SNAKE_CASE>`.
- The manifest is validated by `validateAchievementManifest()` and the drift guard test.
- Precedent: MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC (bumping core submodule pointer).

## Desired Change

- Add one entry to the manifest for the Serial Seller achievement.
- Commit to the core repo and bump the submodule pointer in main-street.
- Coordinate with the producer to register the achievement on Steamworks.

## Key Files (Predicted)

- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — Add `serial-seller` entry
- `core/` (git submodule) — Commit the manifest change
- `.gitmodules` / submodule index — Bump the submodule pointer

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J**: Sell 3 businesses challenge (parent, blocked by this item)
- **MS-0MUNO0M2I004TK04**: Wire Main Street challenges to Steam achievements (parent epic)
- **MS-0MUMAZTAY00515MC**: Precedent for bumping core submodule pointer

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Steamworks backend delay**: If the producer has not yet registered the achievement on Steamworks, the achievement will not unlock for players even after code changes land. This is tracked as a separate action.
- **Scope creep**: Additional achievement metadata (e.g., icons, descriptions) may be desired later; record as a follow-up, not in scope for this item.
- **Submodule conflict**: Unlikely but possible if the core repo has concurrent changes; resolve by rebasing on latest core before bumping.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- This item was already sufficiently defined; no interview questions were asked. The description, scope, and acceptance criteria were clear and actionable.

## Dependency & audit resolution (2026-10-01)

Producer confirmed the Steamworks backend registration (AC2) is not yet done and requires a dependency chain. Two dependency items were created in the core project (CG store — the correct home for Steamworks backend work; worklog does not support cross-store dependency edges, so they are recorded here as cross-project references):

- **CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ** — Create the Steamworks project for Tableau Card Engine
- **CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1** — Register Main Street achievements on the Steamworks backend *(depends on CG-0MUPMJVS90019KSQ)*

**AC2 therefore remains unmet until CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1 completes.** This item carries the `do-not-delegate` tag while externally blocked so the downtime worker does not re-dispatch it.

**Merge state:** the item's work is integrated into `dev`/`origin/dev` as commit `dd11ea4` (core → `d2d1f322`). The stale feature branch (which referenced the superseded core commit `4a287d4`) was reset to `dd11ea4`.

**AC4 call:** the drift guard requires the parent challenge-side mapping from **MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J** (which depends on this item, so no cycle is possible). AC4 is verified at parent integration time; the mapping is present uncommitted in the working tree today and will pass permanently once the parent lands.

## Plan review — 2026-11-05 (verified state)

Verified against the current checkout: main-street `dev` at `f4f083ed`, `core` submodule pinned at `5a16c2fb`, superproject working tree clean.

- **AC1 met** — `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains `achievementId: serial-seller` with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false` (13 entries in total).
- **AC3 met** — the `core` pointer now pins `5a16c2fb`, later than the `d2d1f322` recorded above, and that commit contains the manifest entry.
- **AC4 preconditions satisfied** — the parent mapping (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J) is now **committed**, not uncommitted as stated above: `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` maps all 13 challenges, and the manifest and the game-side mapping agree exactly (13 ↔ 13, no drift in either direction). `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` is the guard that exercises this.
- **AC2 unmet / external** — unchanged: blocked on `CG-0MUPN2I7K003KNL1` (Steamworks backend registration). Not verifiable from the repository.
- **AC5** — no documentation change beyond the manifest entry was identified as required; the existing 12-achievement pattern is followed.
- **AC6** — enforced by the dev-push gate; not re-run by this planning session.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-05 — Plan re-run (effort Extra Small / Low, so decomposition skipped): six review stages run, AC coverage 100% (proceed), stage set to `plan_complete`. Recorded the verified AC state above; no child work items created.

# Finish gate: a lagging engine pin can fail the build itself when `engine:sync` advances past a breaking engine API change

Discovered during **MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4** (AC1 verification of **MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6**), while reproducing the lagging-pin condition. Verification only: nothing was worked around; this item records the gap.

## What happens

`implement.py finish` runs `npm run build`, which starts with `engine:sync`. When the worktree's committed pin lags the engine tracked tip, `engine:sync` advances `./core` to the tip **before** `tsc --noEmit` / `vite build` run — so the build compiles the item's source against an engine the source was never written for.

Reproduced on a throwaway worktree at `a6ef0b7d` (pinned `21bedf7a`; engine `dev` tip `2305f888`), which still uses the pre-rename `hasChoices` manifest flag:

```
engine:sync: core updated 21bedf7a8c → 2305f888d0
src/MainStreetStorylineContentAdapter.ts(88,5): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'hasChoices' does not exist in type 'ContentFieldMapping'.
tests/main-street/MainStreetStorylineContentAdapter.test.ts(194,44): error TS2551: Property 'hasChoices' does not exist on type 'ManifestNode'. Did you mean 'isChoice'?
npm run build → exit 2
```

The build-churn exclusion (`SA-0MVZE164P0048306`) cannot help: it runs **after** a successful build. The same probe at `99489ad8` (pin still `21bedf7a`, but source already at `isChoice`) built cleanly and the exclusion worked as designed.

## Why it matters

The parent epic's user story is that a documentation- or evidence-only item must not be blocked by an unrelated engine bump. Today the re-pin no longer reaches the commit, but the build still runs against the advanced engine first, so an older worktree can fail to build for a reason the item never caused — and the failure arrives as a plain build error, not as an engine-composition condition.

## Options (not decided here)

- (A) Report the condition explicitly: when the pre-build pin lags the engine tip, record it in the finish report and the build-failure message ("build ran against engine <tip>, item pinned <sha> — the advance is not part of the commit"), so the operator can tell an engine-induced build failure from a source failure.
- (B) Build against the pinned composition: restore the pin/gitlink *before* the build and re-sync only when the item itself changes composition (needs producer sign-off — it touches the pin policy `CG-0MVO268500071BPI`).
- (C) Leave as-is and document it as an accepted limitation of syncing at build time.

Option (B) is the closest to remedy C (verify-only `engine:sync`), which the producer already rejected for the finish gate, so it must not be adopted silently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The condition "pre-build pin lags the engine tracked tip and the build failed" is visible in the finish report and the build-failure comment, naming both SHAs.
- [ ] A published limitation note exists in `docs/dev/testing.md` / the implement skill reference if the behaviour is kept.
- [ ] No cache-key or pin-policy change without producer sign-off.

## Plan decision (2026-11-03)

**Option (A) adopted — keep the build-time sync, make the condition explicit — together with the documentation half of Option (C).** The item's own draft AC1 requires exactly this (both SHAs in the finish report *and* the build-failure comment), and AC3 forbids a cache-key or pin-policy change without sign-off. **Option (B) is explicitly not adopted:** it changes build composition and touches pin policy `CG-0MVO268500071BPI`, so it requires producer sign-off and must not be implemented as a side effect of this bug.

- **Repository boundary (precedent Q1=A on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`):** the finish report and the build-failure comment are produced by `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` in **SorraAgents**, which this repository must not edit. # Engine DEVELOPER.md lists reduced motion among the paths that omit deferResourceApplication

Discovered from: MS-0MW20KSEG001DH1X (Turn summary dialog suppressed by reduced motion setting).

## Problem

`core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` (the Tableau-Card-Engine submodule), section *Deferred End-of-Turn Mutation* → bullet *Deferred `processEndOfTurn`*, says:

> Tutorial, reduced-motion and replay paths omit the flag (legacy immediate behaviour, no regression — AC5).

After MS-0MW20KSEG001DH1X the reduced-motion path does **not** omit the flag: the scene (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, `endTurn`) takes the deferred closing path under reduced motion, so the Turn Summary dialog has a `requiresDeferredClosing` result to gate on. Only the tutorial and replay paths still omit it.

## Why it was not fixed in the MS session

- `core` is a git submodule (a separate repository, detached HEAD at the engine pin `5a16c2f`). A working-tree edit leaves the submodule dirty, and `npm run build` runs `engine:sync` (non-soft), which **refuses** to sync a dirty submodule ("never clobber") — every later build in this repo would fail.
- A local commit inside the submodule is discarded by the next `engine:sync` (it checks out the remote target), so the fix would silently vanish.
- The engine checkout has no worklog (`wl` there reports "not initialized"), and pushing to the engine repo's `dev` is not authorised from a game-repo session.

## Fix

In the Tableau-Card-Engine repository, amend that bullet so only the tutorial and replay paths are named as flag-omitting, and state that the reduced-motion path takes the deferred closing so a game's Turn Summary gate can present its summary dialog (cross-reference the game-side behaviour).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` no longer claims the reduced-motion path omits `deferResourceApplication`.
2. The bullet names the tutorial and replay paths as the immediate/flag-omitting ones and explains why the reduced-motion path is deferred.
3. No code change is required; the engine's documentation guards (if any) still pass.

# Intake Brief — Gate specialization-skill effects by staff type (MS-0MW3LTMHT001PRDT)

## Problem statement

Specialization skills are assigned from a global 16-skill pool regardless of a staff card's type, and the street-wide folds aggregate every employed member's skills. As a result, a **business-staff** member can hold a **management-company-scope** skill (Cost Cutter, Negotiator, Brand Ambassador, the four incident-mitigation skills, the Town Gossip baseline) and leak a player/street-scope effect, while a **management-company** member can draw **business-scope** skills (Chef, DJ, Networker, …) that can never resolve. The shipped behaviour therefore contradicts the two-type model reconciled in `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` (and GDD D.4.8), where a skill takes effect only from a member whose type matches the skill's scope.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — needs specialization skills to be a meaningful, type-consistent hiring signal: a business-staff hire improves its business, a management-company hire improves the player's turn, never an unexplained cross-scope leak.
- **Game designer / balance owner** — needs the shipped behaviour to match the documented two-type model so balance tuning and the skill catalog are trustworthy.
- **Implementing developer** — needs a deterministic, testable gate that preserves seeded reproducibility and existing save compatibility.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a skill held by a business-staff member to affect only that business, so that hiring decisions match the two-type model.
- As a game designer, I want assignment to draw skills consistent with a staff card's type, so that no card can hold an effect it can never realise.
- As a developer, I want the seeded assignment stream to stay deterministic, so that same seed ⇒ same game is preserved.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Scope gate (behavioural).** A business-staff member holding a management-company-scope skill (Cost Cutter, Negotiator, Brand Ambassador, any of the four incident-mitigation skills, or the Town Gossip baseline) produces **no** player- or street-scope effect; equally, a management-company member holding a business-scope skill produces **no** per-business buff. The Operations Manager salary discount remains a business-staff effect applied to its employing member.
2. **Type-consistent assignment (deterministic).** Business staff draw only business-scope skills; management-company staff draw only player-scope skills plus the Town Gossip baseline. The stacking caps (≤1 income-boost, ≤1 reputation-boost beyond baseline) remain per-member and type-neutral.
3. **Determinism preserved.** The assignment stream stays seeded and reproducible (same seed ⇒ same assignments); existing determinism tests continue to pass, and new determinism tests cover the type-consistent draw.
4. **Documentation updated.** `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` records that the follow-up gap is closed (or removes the follow-up section), and the GDD D.4.8 / `card-catalog.md` cross-references stay consistent. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. **Validation.** At least one automated test proves the scope gate (both leak directions) and the type-consistent assignment; the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Preserve determinism.** The assignment RNG stays the dedicated `createSeededRng(numericSeed ^ 0x5eed)` stream; do not perturb the main RNG stream (deck shuffles, market draws, challenges).
- **Preserve save compatibility.** Skills persist as stable id arrays; the staff type is derived from `employedAtSlot` and must not require a new stored field.
- **No new skills or magnitude changes.** The 16-skill catalog and its magnitudes are unchanged; this item only gates effects and constrains assignment.
- **Two staff types only.** Business staff = has `employedAtSlot`; management-company staff = no `employedAtSlot` (GDD D.4.2/D.4.8). No third type or skill flag.
- **Documentation-only gap closure.** Update the follow-up section of `specialization-skills.md` to mark the gap closed; do not re-open the two-type design.
- **UK English** throughout.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — `STAFF_SKILL_CATALOG` (16 skills, 4 categories); `assignSkillsToApplicant(rng)` draws from the **global** pool and always adds the Town Gossip baseline; `assignStaffApplicantSkills(state)` seeds assignments across the staff deck and market row. The catalog carries no scope/type field today.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `getEmployedSpecializationSkills(state)` flattens **every** employed member's skills (street-wide); `getEmployedSpecializationSkillsForBusiness(state, slot)` flattens only that slot's members; `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs`, `computeIncidentSkillBuffs`, `computeStreetOngoingCostReductionPct`, `computeRefreshCostDiscount`, `computeStaffSalaryDiscount`, `computeReputationGainMultiplier`, etc. translate skills to effects.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts`, `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — consume the street-wide and per-business aggregations.
- `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` — § *Shipped cross-type assignments — reconciliation follow-up* documents the two gaps and states they are not yet fixed; the skill table already classifies 8 business-staff and 8 management-company skills.
- Existing tests: `staff-skill-assignment.test.ts`, `staff-skill-assignment-state.test.ts` (determinism, stacking, baseline), `staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts`, `staff-effect-scoping.test.ts`, `specialization-skills-two-types.test.ts` (doc contract).

## Desired change

1. **Scope gate.** Make street-wide/player-scope effect folds read only management-company members' skills, and per-business folds read only business-scope skills from the employing business's members — so a skill is inert when its scope does not match its holder's type. Keep the Operations Manager salary discount as a business-staff effect.
2. **Type-consistent assignment.** Draw business-scope skills for business staff and player-scope skills for management-company staff, always keeping the Town Gossip baseline on management-company cards. Preserve the per-member stacking caps and the seeded, reproducible stream.
3. **Docs + tests.** Update the `specialization-skills.md` follow-up section (gap closed/removed) and GDD/card-catalog cross-references; add determinism and scope-gate tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — skill scope classification + type-consistent `assignSkillsToApplicant` / `assignStaffApplicantSkills`.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — scope-gated `getEmployedSpecializationSkills` / `getEmployedSpecializationSkillsForBusiness`; per-business fold gating.
- `src/MainStreetEngineEvents.ts` — incident/reputation folds consume gated skills.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — Negotiator refresh discount consumes gated skills.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` / `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` — ongoing-cost and salary folds consume gated skills.
- `docs/game/specialization-skills.md` — follow-up section closed; cross-reference consistency.
- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4.8) / `docs/game/card-catalog.md` — cross-reference consistency.
- `tests/main-street/staff-skill-assignment.test.ts`, `staff-skill-assignment-state.test.ts`, `staff-effect-scoping.test.ts`, `staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts` — scope-gate and determinism coverage.

## Related work

- **MS-0MW20VBSZ003A01O** — Staff impact (epic; completed). Parent of the documentation work that discovered this gap.

- Docs: `docs/game/specialization-skills.md`, `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (Appendix D.4), `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (§ Staff Cards).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — determinism regression:** changing the candidate pool per type alters the seeded stream; *mitigation:* dedicated tests assert same-seed reproducibility across both types, and the salt/main-stream separation is preserved.
- **Risk — partial gate:** gating only the assignment leaves a stale save or hand-built fixture with a cross-type skill leaking; *mitigation:* the scope gate is enforced at the aggregation site, not only at assignment, and tests cover a cross-type skill held by both staff types.
- **Risk — Operations Manager mis-scope:** it is a cost skill but a business-staff effect; *mitigation:* explicit AC/test that its salary discount applies only from the employing business's member.
- **Risk — scope creep:** temptation to re-tune magnitudes or rebuild the catalog; *mitigation:* catalog magnitudes are out of scope and unchanged.

- **Assumption:** the skill-scope classification is the one already recorded in `specialization-skills.md` (8 business / 8 management-company).
- **Assumption:** the existing determinism and doc-contract tests remain the acceptance baseline.

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (work item description plus the reconciled `specialization-skills.md` follow-up section, GDD D.4.8, and the source code) fully determines the problem, scope, acceptance criteria, constraints, and key files. The discovering item MS-0MW2XMB0P002D95K already recorded the two gaps and the producer-approved two-type model, so the intake proceeds without an interview.

**Headline:** `run_tests.py` cannot parse Vitest's default-reporter failure output, so a real browser-mode assertion failure is reported as `unparsed_failure` (gate `reason: unparsed`) and no `test-failure` work item is created — the operator is told the *command or configuration* is wrong when the *code* is at fault.

## Problem statement

The test runner's Node failure parser only understands TAP (`not ok N - <name>`) output, so a failing Vitest test yields **zero** structured failure records. This repo's Vitest projects (`npm test` for `unit`/`unit-cli`, and `npx vitest run --project browser …` for the serial browser suite) emit Vitest's default-reporter format: `FAIL  |browser (chromium)| <file> > <suite> > <test>`, a `× <test name>` tree marker, an `AssertionError`/cause line, and `Test Files 1 failed (1)` / `Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2)` summary lines. None of those match the parser, so `failures == []`, the suite is classified `unparsed_failure`, and the finish gate reports `reason: unparsed` with an empty `Failures:` list instead of naming the failing test.

## Users

- **Implementing agent (primary).** As an agent finishing a work item, I need the test gate to name the failing browser test so triage can open a `[test-failure]` item and I can fix the code rather than hunt through a 40 s browser log tail.
  - `As the implement skill finishing MS-x, when a browser assertion fails I get reason: test_failure and a test name, not reason: unparsed.`
- **Operator/producer (secondary).** As the producer reading a red gate report, I need the reason to distinguish "fix the code" (`test_failure`) from "the command/configuration is broken" (`unparsed`), so I send the work to the right place.
  - `As the producer, a red browser run tells me which test failed and which file to inspect.`
- **Triage skill (downstream).** As triage, I need structured failure records (`test_name`, `stdout_excerpt`, `stack_trace`) so `check_or_create.py` can create or match the existing `test-failure` item instead of falling back to a `<suite exited 1>` placeholder.
  - `As triage, one failure record per failing Vitest test is enough to create the [test-failure] item with the real test name.`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A Vitest **browser-mode** failure output (default reporter: `FAIL  |browser (chromium)| <file> > <suite> > <test>`, `× <test name>`, assertion/cause lines, `Test Files … failed` summary) parses into at least one structured failure record whose `test_name` contains the failing file and test name, with a non-empty `stdout_excerpt` — pinned by a regression test built from the evidence in this item.
- [ ] The same parser handles the **unit/unit-cli** Vitest form (`FAIL  |unit| <file> > <suite> > <test>`) and the browser file-tree form, de-duplicates a test reported in both places, and never emits a record for the `Test Files …`/`Tests …` summary lines.
- [ ] With a parsed Vitest failure present, `run_suite` reports `failures` non-empty and **no** `notice_code` (`unparsed_failure`/`killed` not set), so the shared classifier (`gate_reason.py`) and `implement.py finish` report `reason: test_failure`; the end-to-end assertion is pinned by a test that runs a Vitest-shaped result through the gate classifier.
- [ ] Genuinely unparsable non-zero runs still classify as `unparsed_failure` (the existing Playwright/`ENOSPC` and inode-exhaustion fixtures keep their current classification), and TAP (`node --test`) and pytest parsing are unchanged.
- [ ] The audit skill's suite-failure path uses the same Vitest parser (it currently imports only `parse_node_failures`), so the audit does not report a `<suite exited 1>` placeholder for a Vitest assertion failure.
- [ ] The change ships with the regression tests above passing in the repo that owns the code, and all related documentation is updated (test-skill reference failure-parsing/notice sections, plus any statement that Vitest failures are unparsed).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repository ownership.** The code lives in the shared skills repo (`SorraAgents`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`), not in this checkout — the same pattern as MS-0MVZJ3175002WZO2 (MS item, change committed on SorraAgents `dev`). The brief therefore names SorraAgents paths; no `.pi/` or `skill/` tree exists in `tce-main-street` to edit.
- **No command changes.** Parse the text the runner already receives (`npx vitest run …`, `npm --silent test`); do not inject `--reporter=json` into suite commands, because that would alter gate evidence, cache fingerprints and the documented "one Vitest invocation, same flags" contract.
- **Precedence contract is fixed:** structured failures always win over infrastructure notice codes, and `state_changed_during_run` still wins over everything.
- **No masking.** The parser must not turn an unparsed infrastructure failure into a `test_failure`: absence of recognised Vitest markers must keep the current `unparsed_failure` behaviour.
- Existing failure-record contract is fixed by consumers: `test_name`, `stdout_excerpt` (≤1000 chars), `stack_trace` (triage `check_or_create.py`, audit).

## Existing state

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` routes per command: `"pytest" in cmd → parse_pytest_failures()`, everything else → `parse_node_failures()`. Neither handles the Vitest default reporter; `parse_node_failures` is TAP-only (`_NODE_NOT_OK_RE = ^not ok …`).
- `run_suite` sets `notice_code = unparsed_failure` when `failures` is empty and the return code is positive; `killed` when negative. `implement.py`'s `_adapt_guarded_result`/`_gate_failure_kind` then map that to `reason: unparsed`.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` imports `parse_node_failures` for non-pytest suite commands and emits a `<suite exited N>` placeholder when nothing parses.
- Out of scope: `implement.py`'s legacy `_finalize_test_result` line-grep path (used only when the guarded runner is unavailable) already yields non-empty failure lines for Vitest output; it is left unchanged.
- Documented in `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` (notice codes / precedence) and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (gate reasons/table) — both describe `unparsed_failure` as "the command or configuration is the problem".
- Evidence from MS-0MW3O2ODT007ZJGL: a failing `tests/**/*.browser.test.ts` run printed `FAIL  |browser (chromium)|`, `AssertionError`, `× …` markers and the failed summary, while the runner reported `success: false`, `notice_codes: ['unparsed_failure']`, `failures: []`, and `implement.py finish` reported `reason: unparsed`.

## Desired change

- Add a Vitest failure parser (e.g. `parse_vitest_failures(output)`) that recognises the Failed-Tests block (`FAIL  |<project>| <file> > <suite> > <test>`) and the per-file tree markers (`× <test name>` under `❯ |<project>| <file> (N tests | M failed)`), attaching the following error/code-frame text as `stdout_excerpt`/`stack_trace`, de-duplicated per test.
- Route Vitest commands to it (a small `is_vitest_command(cmd)` helper beside `is_pytest_command`), keeping TAP and pytest routing intact.
- Reuse the same parser in the audit runner's non-pytest path.
- Keep classification untouched: non-empty `failures` ⇒ no notice code ⇒ `test_failure`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Needs a Vitest failure parser, a `is_vitest_command` routing helper, and per-command parser selection in `run_suite`.
- `skill/test_runner.py` — Needs `is_vitest_command` (sibling of `is_pytest_command`) if routing is to be shared with `test_cache.py`/audit.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Needs the Vitest parser in the non-pytest branch instead of TAP-only parsing.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_vitest_parser.py` (new) — Regression tests for browser-mode and unit-mode output, de-duplication, summary-line rejection, and unchanged TAP/pytest behaviour.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py` — Needs a case proving a Vitest failure produces failures (no `unparsed_failure` notice) while the ENOSPC fixture stays unparsed.
- `skill/shared/tests/gate_failure_fixtures.py` — Needs a captured browser-mode failure fixture (the evidence block from this item) for reuse across gate/classifier tests.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — Update the failure-parsing and notice-code sections (state which formats parse and that Vitest failures are no longer unparsed).
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — Update the gate-reason table entry for `unparsed` if it asserts browser failures are unparsed.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the Vitest default reporter is the only output shape in scope (no `--reporter=verbose`/`--reporter=junit` overrides in this repo's `suiteCommands` or groups). A custom reporter would still be unparsed — recorded as a follow-up, not scope.
- **Assumption:** the fix belongs in the shared skill repo and is tracked by this MS item (precedent MS-0MVZJ3175002WZO2). If the producer wants a separate SA item, that is a tracking change, not a design change.
- **Risk:** an over-broad regex could match summary lines or prose and fabricate failures — mitigated by an explicit "no record for `Test Files`/`Tests` summary lines" test.
- **Risk:** browser output interleaves worker/RPC noise; parsing must be tolerant of ANSI colour codes and the ASCII-`x` transliteration seen in captured logs.
- **Risk (scope creep):** JSON-reporter integration, Vitest 4 reporter changes, and flaky-vs-real classification are separate opportunities; record them as linked items rather than widening this fix.
- Multi-line assertion blocks can be large — truncation to the existing 1000-char excerpt bound keeps records bounded.
- **Measurable outcome:** the evidence run's captured output (replayed as a fixture) produces ≥ 1 failure record and gate `reason: test_failure`; the ENOSPC/inode-exhaustion fixtures still produce `reason: unparsed`.

## Related work

- `MS-0MW3O2ODT007ZJGL` — Tests: auto-advance end-turn and guard browser tests (discovery source; the failing browser run).
- `MS-0MW08THR2000YXEO` — `[test-failure] hud-total-counting-live.browser.test.ts …` (shows the evidence shape that the parser must recognise; its item was created without a parsable runner failure).
- `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR` — Verify AC3: gate failures distinguish timeout, kill and queue wait (owns the notice-code contract and the `unparsed` classification).
- `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` — test-cache/timeout epic whose SA-item C introduced the `unparsed` classification.

- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — the documented failure-classification contract.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Where does the fix live — this repo or the shared skills repo? — **Answer (repo evidence, no producer input needed):** `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` in `SorraAgents` (the only copy of the runner; `tce-main-street` has no `skill/` tree and only a `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` profile map). Precedent: MS-0MVZJ3175002WZO2 ("Implemented and pushed to SorraAgents `dev`"). Source: filesystem inspection + worklog comment.
- **Q:** Is the unit/unit-cli Vitest project also affected, or only browser mode? — **Answer (source inspection):** the same parser gap applies to every Vitest command (the default reporter shape is identical apart from the `|<project>|` label), so the parser is written once and covers both; browser mode is the pinned evidence. Source: `run_tests.py` parser routing + `package.json` test scripts.
- **Q:** Should the runner switch Vitest to a JSON reporter for exact failures? — **Answer (documented assumption, not taken):** no — it would change gate evidence, cache fingerprints and the documented "same flags" contract; text parsing matches the existing parser architecture and the observed output. Recorded as a follow-up opportunity if text parsing proves brittle. Source: `scripts/run-tests.ts` / `core/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` header contracts.

# Loan payoff dialog: carry the payoff across a paused closing

discovered-from:MS-0MW3SN58E009HC84

## Goal (user story)

As a player whose loan retires in a turn that also pauses on an event-choice
dialog (or a bankruptcy bailout offer), I want to still see the debt-free
congratulation once the pause resolves, so that no payoff goes unnotified.

## Context

`MS-0MW3SN58E009HC84` presents the payoff dialog in the closing presentation
slot (`MainStreetLoanPayoffModel.presentLoanPayoffDialogs`), after the closing
animations and ahead of the End of Turn summary. Two pauses resolve **after**
that slot, so their payoffs are currently never presented:

- **Event choice**: `processEndOfTurn` retires the loan and then pauses
  (`choicePending`) before `finishTurnPresentation` reaches the presentation
  slot. The resume path (`onEventChoice` → `finishDeferredEndOfTurn`) builds a
  fresh result that does **not** carry `loanPayoffs`.
- **Bankruptcy bailout**: the deferred result pauses on the loan offer
  (`pendingLoanOffer`); `onLoanOfferChoice` resumes through
  `completeDeferredClosingTail`, which never presents payoffs. A declined offer
  ends the run, so game over correctly wins there; an **accepted** offer
  continues the run with no congratulation.

The paused path never duplicates a dialog (there is only one presentation slot),
so this is a *missed* notification, not a duplicate.

## Desired change

Carry the paused closing's `loanPayoffs` into the resumed flow (the same
pattern `pendingBankingHint` uses for the banking hint) and present them via
the existing `presentLoanPayoffDialogs` sequencer on the continuing resume
path — never on a resume that ends the run (game over wins).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. An event-choice-paused closing that retired a loan presents exactly one
   congratulation when the choice resolves, and never two.
2. A bailout-paused closing where the seat accepts an offer (the run continues)
   presents exactly one congratulation; a declined offer (the run ends)
   presents the game-over overlay and no congratulation.
3. The dialog still appears only after the closing presentation and never
   alongside another modal.
4. Unit tests cover both pause paths, including the no-duplicate rule.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — carry the payoffs across
  `presentEventChoiceDialog` / `presentLoanOfferDialog` and present them on the
  continuing resume.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanPayoffModel.ts` — `presentLoanPayoffDialogs`
  (reused unchanged).
- `tests/main-street/loan-payoff-turn-flow.test.ts` — the pause/resume cases.

## Constraints

- Presentation only: no engine, arithmetic, wallet or RNG change.
- One modal at a time; the summary/bailout/event-choice pacing is unchanged.

# Enable bank loans in competitive play

Enable the human player's **mid-game bank loan** entry point in competitive
mode: the competitive Turn Summary panel's `[ Bank Loan ]` button, which is
today always disabled ("Bank loans are not available in competitive play
yet."), becomes interactive for the player's own seat, following the exact
single-player flow (option selector → take → re-render). The AI keeps its
bailout-only loan policy; bailout, repayment, HUD obligation and persistence
already work per-seat in competitive mode and are unchanged.

## Problem statement

The Bank Loans epic (MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG, shipped v0.1.23) delivered the loan
engine, per-seat competitive bailout, and the single-player End of Turn
summary entry point. The competitive Turn Summary panel (MS-0MVRNV9Y8008IKGK)
was deliberately shipped with `[ Bank Loan ]` **disabled** — a static
"not available in competitive play yet" hint — behind a per-seat-capable seam,
deferring per-seat mid-game loans. Today a competitive player can never choose
to take a loan during play, while an AI opponent hitting `coins < 0`
auto-accepts a bailout loan, so the player sees the AI borrow while their own
seat cannot — the asymmetry this item removes.

## Users

- **Human player, competitive mode** — "In competitive play I want the same
  Bank Loan affordance I have in single-player — the [ Bank Loan ] button on
  the Turn Summary, offered to my own seat when I am short of cash — so I can
  buy my way past a cash crunch exactly as an AI opponent does."
- **Producer / designer** — "Competitive loans must reuse the shipped engine
  and single-player UI patterns, not fork them; the AI bailout-only policy
  stays as decided (parent Q3 = A)."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Player-own-seat loan button.** In a competitive game (N ≥ 2) with
  `config.loansEnabled`, the Turn Summary panel's `[ Bank Loan ]` button is
  **enabled exactly when the human player's seat may borrow** (same rules as
  single-player: loans enabled, no active loan on that seat, a non-empty
  configured menu). Pressing it opens the existing mid-game loan selector
  driven by `config.loanOptions`; the disabled state otherwise shows a
  reason-specific hint (loans-disabled / active-loan obligation / no-options)
  instead of the static "not available in competitive play yet" copy.
- **AC2 — Per-seat correctness.** The loan taken from the competitive panel is
  booked to the **human seat** (explicit `ownerId` = the human seat id, via
  `findHumanSeatId`), never to the transient `activePlayerId` of a
  round-robin turn that may differ at the shared-day close; principal, log row
  and ledger credit match the single-player take exactly, and the loan is
  AP-neutral and undoable through the command surface (`takeLoanCommand` with
  the owner forwarded). A human seat already repaying a loan cannot take a
  second one (one-active-loan rule, unmodified).
- **AC3 — No regressions to shipped paths.** AI seats keep the bailout-only
  policy (no proactive AI lending — parent Q3 = A). The per-seat competitive
  bailout offer/accept/decline, standing repayment pass, HUD obligation
  readout (single-player + competitive scoreboard), loan payoff dialogs,
  save/load v3 round-trip and `loansEnabled: false` hard no-op all behave
  exactly as today, verified by the existing loan test inventory staying
  green.
- **AC4 — Testing/validation.** Tests cover: (a) the descriptor for the
  human seat drives the button's enabled/disabled state in the competitive
  panel, (b) an accepted take credits the human seat only and survives a
  re-render of the same `TurnResult`, (c) an active loan disables the button
  with the obligation hint, (d) `loansEnabled: false` / empty-menu keep it
  disabled, and (e) the mid-game take during a save/load round-trip.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  change: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§5.1 two-entry-points
  paragraph currently states the competitive panel ships disabled "so per-seat
  mid-game loans arrive later"), in-game help copy where it mentions the
  Turn Summary `[ Bank Loan ]` button, code comments on the
  `COMPETITIVE_BANK_LOAN_HINT` / `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog` seam, and
  any relevant docs-site entry (e.g. `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Reuse, don't fork** — the competitive panel keeps its per-seat model and
  single `[ Bank Loan ]` + `[ Next Turn ]` action row; enabling the button
  reuses the shipped `buildTurnSummaryLoanDescriptor(state, ownerId)`,
  `buildLoanSelectorModel`, `showLoanSelectorDialog` and `takeLoan`/command
  machinery rather than adding a parallel loan UI.
- **Human seat only** — the button is keyed to the human (player-controlled)
  seat; AI seats never get a proactive loan affordance (parent Q3 = A).
- **No engine-rule changes** — loan menu, interest, repayment, one-active-loan
  and shortfall semantics are untouched; this item wires an existing, already
  per-seat-capable path through the competitive presentation layer.
- **No action point and AP-neutral** — the take must not decrement
  `actionsRemaining`; the existing `takeLoan` no-AP rule already guarantees
  this and must not be loosened.
- **Non-blocking presentation** — a failing model build, an unbuildable
  descriptor/selector, or a scene without dialog support must never strand
  the shared day (existing gate contract).
- **Priority `critical` retained** — operator-set at dispatch; kept per the
  precedence rule even though the change is a net-new feature (classification
  would suggest `medium`/`high`) — flagged for producer re-confirmation.

## Existing state

- Engine is competitive-capable: `canTakeLoan`/`takeLoan` accept an `ownerId`
  and validate per seat (`src/MainStreetLoans.ts`), `creditLoanPrincipal`
  handles the `PlayerRecord` wallet plus the bound-seat `resourceBank` mirror
  (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`), and `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`
  offers the human seat a **pending** bailout (surfaced as
  `TurnResult.pendingLoanOffer`, resolved via `resolveCompetitiveLoanOffer`)
  while AI seats auto-accept the largest option inline.
- The competitive Turn Summary panel is built by `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`) and presented by
  `presentCompetitiveTurnSummaryGate` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`),
  which calls `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog(summary, advanceOnce)` **without**
  `onBankLoanAction`.
- `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`)
  renders `[ Bank Loan ]` always muted/inert with
  `COMPETITIVE_BANK_LOAN_HINT = 'Bank loans are not available in competitive
  play yet.'` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`) and ends with
  `void onBankLoanAction;` — the seam is accepted but intentionally unwired.
- Single-player reference flow: `presentTurnSummaryGate` builds a
  `loanDescriptor`, passes it to `showTurnSummaryDialog`, whose `[ Bank Loan ]`
  handler builds `buildLoanSelectorModel(s.state)`, opens `showLoanSelectorDialog`,
  `confirmSelection` runs `takeLoanCommand(state, optionIndex, { allowDuringClosing: true })`
  through the undo manager, and re-presents the summary from the same
  `TurnResult` (`MS-0MVXYCKFE000VF76`).
- `takeLoanCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts`) currently forwards
  `ownerId = undefined` (the acting seat) to `takeLoan`; competitive takes must
  forward the human seat id instead (AC2).
- Docs: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §5.1 "Two entry points" states
  the competitive panel ships disabled "until per-seat mid-game loans arrive";
  help copy in `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` already refers to the Turn
  Summary `[ Bank Loan ]` button (single-player framing).
- No loan work item is open on this gap (duplicate check performed — all prior
  bank-loan items are `completed`; this is the deferred competitive seam).

## Desired change

1. **Descriptor for the human seat.** In
   `presentCompetitiveTurnSummaryGate` (or the dialog seam), resolve the human
   seat id (`findHumanSeatId`) and build
   `buildTurnSummaryLoanDescriptor(state, humanSeatId)` (loans-disabled /
   active-loan / no-options / enabled) instead of the static hint; pass
   `onBankLoanAction` keyed to that seat into
   `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog(summary, onNextTurn, onBankLoanAction)`.
2. **Enable the button in `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog`.** Mirror the
   single-player button: interactive in normal colour when the descriptor says
   enabled, muted/inert with the descriptor's reason-specific hint otherwise;
   drop the `COMPETITIVE_BANK_LOAN_HINT` static copy (keep the exported
   constant or replace with descriptor-driven text). Wire the pointer handler
   to open the per-seat mid-game selector (via `buildLoanSelectorModel` /
   `showLoanSelectorDialog`) and re-present the same `TurnResult` panel after
   the take, exactly like the single-player panel (`returnToSummary` pattern).
3. **Per-seat take.** Ensure the take is booked to the human seat: extend
   `takeLoanCommand` to forward an `ownerId` (or add a per-seat variant)
   calling `takeLoan(state, optionIndex, humanSeatId, { allowDuringClosing: true })`,
   executed through the shared undo manager; the selector's confirm path in the
   competitive panel must pass the human seat id.
4. **Docs & copy refresh.** Update `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`
   §5.1 (competitive panel is now interactive for the player's seat), the
   in-game help text and any UX-doc mention; update code comments that state
   the competitive button is "deliberately never wired".

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Proactive (non-bailout) AI lending — parent Q3 = A decision stands.
- Per-seat loan buttons inside each panel row — the panel keeps its single
  action row; the button is the human seat's.
- Any change to loan menu, interest, repayment, one-active-loan, shortfall or
  bailout semantics.
- Score/reputation effects of loans (existing follow-up space, not this item).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — replace the static
  `COMPETITIVE_BANK_LOAN_HINT` ("…not available in competitive play yet.") with
  descriptor-driven copy (or keep the export for the disabled fallback);
  `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` gains the human seat's loan state if the panel
  needs to render it.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` —
  `presentCompetitiveTurnSummaryGate`: resolve `findHumanSeatId`, build the
  descriptor, pass `onBankLoanAction(seatId)` into
  `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog`; the handler opens the selector and
  re-presents the same closing.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` —
  `showCompetitiveTurnSummaryDialog`: enable/wire `[ Bank Loan ]` per the
  descriptor; reuse `buildLoanSelectorModel` + `showLoanSelectorDialog` +
  `takeLoanCommand` confirm path (single-player `returnToSummary` pattern);
  replace the always-disabled rendering and `void onBankLoanAction;`.
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `takeLoanCommand`: forward an `ownerId`
  (defaulting to the acting seat) so competitive takes book to the human seat.
- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — unchanged (already per-seat); only verification.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanSelectorModel.ts` —
  `buildTurnSummaryLoanDescriptor(state, ownerId)` already accepts the seat;
  confirm the competitive gate passes the human seat id. Possibly unchanged.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — §5.1 "Two entry points": describe
  the competitive panel's now-interactive button for the player's seat.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — help copy: mention the competitive Turn
  Summary `[ Bank Loan ]` for the player's seat.
- `tests/main-street/` — **new/updated**: competitive panel descriptor-gated
  button tests, per-seat take + re-render test, active-loan disables, loans-off
  / empty-menu disabled states, save/load round-trip mid-game take; existing
  `MainStreetLoanCompetitive.test.ts`, `MainStreetLoanOverlay.test.ts` /
  `.browser.test.ts`, `turn-summary-bank-loan*.test.ts` remain green.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG — Bank Loans** (completed, shipped v0.1.23). Parent
  epic: engine, config, takeLoan command, repayment, per-seat bailout, HUD,
  persistence v3, docs. Its Non-goals explicitly deferred the Turn Summary
  wiring into competitive per-seat loans; all six recorded producer decisions
  (Q1 one loan, Q2 option menu, Q3 bailout-only AI, Q4 engine+UI now /
  dialog wiring later, Q5 largest option, Q6 unconditional repayment) bind
  this item.
- **MS-0MVRNV9Y8008IKGK — Competitive summary rows end-to-end** (completed).
  Built `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary` and the gate; the loans seam
  (`(seatId?: number) => void`) was shaped here and left unwired.
- **MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI — End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode**
  (completed). Competitive dialog shell that already accepts
  `onBankLoanAction`.
- **MS-0MVPWSQMG004198C — Wire Bank Loan button into Turn Summary dialog**
  (completed). The single-player wiring this item mirrors (selector +
  `takeLoanCommand` + re-render from same result).
- **MS-0MVPWSAMH005LV9R — Competitive seat bailout parity** (completed).
  Per-seat offer evaluation; human seat keeps a pending offer for the UI, AI
  auto-accepts — unchanged by this item.
- **MS-0MVXYCIU00053HL1 — Loan eligibility in the deferred-closing window**
  (completed). `allowDuringClosing` / `isDeferredClosingPause` — the
  competitive Turn Summary gate is the same window.
- **MS-0MVXYCJVU000QBK1 / MS-0MVXYCKFE000VF76 — mid-game selector + re-render
  from same result** (completed). The single-player patterns reused verbatim.
- **MS-0MVRNW5JT0046QI3 — Competitive summary invariants** (completed).
  Row/elimination invariants the re-render must keep.
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping open/completed item; the closest
  (turn-summary wiring items) are single-player and completed.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption A1 — scope is the proactive mid-game button.** "Enable bank
  loans for the player in competitive play" is read as the competitive Turn
  Summary `[ Bank Loan ]` entry point for the human seat — the only player
  loan path missing in competitive (bailout already works per seat, verified
  in `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures` + `presentLoanOfferDialog`). If instead
  the reporter observed a *broken* human bailout, the investigation above
  shows it is wired; a follow-up bug item would be raised rather than folding
  it here. Assumption recorded so the producer can veto at review.
- **Assumption A2 — human seat only.** Enabled for the player's own seat via
  explicit `ownerId`; AI proactive lending stays out of scope (parent Q3 = A).
- **Assumption A3 — button reflects the human seat.** The panel's single
  `[ Bank Loan ]` button is keyed to the human seat's obligation (the seat the
  player controls), mirroring single-player descriptor semantics.
- **Assumption A4 — priority.** `critical` was set at dispatch; the change is
  a net-new feature (classification would suggest `medium`/`high`). Retained
  per the operator-precedence rule; flagged for re-confirmation.
- **Risk — acting-seat vs human-seat mismatch.** Competitive turns round-robin
  `activePlayerId`; at the shared-day close it may not be the human seat, so a
  default-owner take could credit the wrong seat. Mitigation: explicit
  `findHumanSeatId` + forwarded `ownerId` (AC2), tested.
- **Risk — re-render drift.** Post-take re-presentation reuses the same
  `TurnResult` against live state; the competitive builder
  (`buildCompetitiveTurnSummary`) must reflect the new loan/HUD obligation
  without resurrecting eliminated seats or ghost rows. Mitigation: reuse the
  single-player `returnToSummary` pattern plus the existing
  `MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard` loan readout; regression tests.
- **Risk — presentation no-ops.** An unbuildable descriptor/selector must keep
  the current disabled/hint behaviour, never strand the shared day
  (existing gate contract). Mitigation: descriptor try/catch mirroring
  single-player.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Per-row loan buttons, proactive AI lending and
  loan-related scoring changes are natural "while we're here" additions; each
  is a Non-goal here (consistent with the parent epic's Non-goals).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No interviewer round was run. The seed context ("loans not available for the
player in competitive play, but the AI can take them out — enable them for the
player") plus conclusive repo evidence and the parent epic's recorded producer
decisions (Q1–Q6, MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG) were sufficient to draft this brief;
the two scope calls (A1 mid-game button only; A2 human seat only) are recorded
as **documented assumptions** above rather than invented requirements, so the
producer can veto at review. Should the producer prefer a different reading
(e.g. per-row buttons or proactive AI loans), the brief is revised
idempotently.
